_meta.note: Source of truth for the Wine Holidays calendar feed. Edit this file, run `node build.mjs`, commit the regenerated .ics.

ruleTypes.fixed: Same calendar date every year. { month, day }
ruleTypes.nth_weekday: Nth weekday of a month. { month, weekday, n } where n = 1..4 or -1 for last
ruleTypes.computed: Needs real date math, cannot be expressed as an iCal RRULE. { fn }

confidence.high: Confirmed by the organising body, or a legally/traditionally fixed date
confidence.medium: Several independent calendars agree, no official organiser found
confidence.low: Sources disagree, or only one source found — check before relying on it

holidays.name: St Vincent's Day (Winemakers' Patron Saint)
holidays.description: Feast of St Vincent, patron saint of winegrowers. Marked as Vincencovo in Slovenia and Croatia, and by the Saint-Vincent Tournante procession that rotates between villages in Burgundy.

holidays.name: International Port Wine Day
holidays.description: A day for Portugal's fortified wine from the Douro. Note there are two competing Port days — this one and 10 September. Both are in this calendar.

holidays.name: International Furmint Day
holidays.description: Hungary's flagship white grape, behind both dry Tokaj wines and sweet Tokaji Aszu.

holidays.name: Trifon Zarezan — Day of Winegrowers and Winemakers
holidays.description: Bulgaria's vine-pruning festival honouring St Tryphon, patron of winemakers. The Orthodox church moved the feast to 1 February in 1968, but the country still keeps the growers' day on 14 February.

holidays.name: International Syrah Day
holidays.description: The Northern Rhone's great red grape, known as Shiraz in Australia (which has its own separate day in July).

holidays.name: Global Drink Wine Day
holidays.description: A general-purpose excuse. No grape, no region, no rules.

holidays.name: Open That Bottle Night
holidays.description: Started by the Wall Street Journal's wine columnists: the night you finally drink the special bottle you have been saving for an occasion that never comes.

holidays.name: International Mulled Wine Day
holidays.description: A late-winter send-off for gluhwein, vin chaud and glogg.

holidays.name: International Riesling Day
holidays.description: Riesling's birthday — the date of the first written record of the grape, in a 1435 cellar inventory.

holidays.name: Washington Wine Month
holidays.description: Month-long promotion of Washington State wine.

holidays.name: World Vermouth Day
holidays.description: Aromatised, fortified wine — Turin, Chambery and Reus all have a claim.

holidays.name: Tannat Day
holidays.description: Uruguay's signature red, originally from Madiran in south-west France. Promoted by Wines of Uruguay.

holidays.name: World Malbec Day
holidays.description: Marks 17 April 1853, when Argentine president Sarmiento formally set out to build the country's wine industry — with Malbec at the centre. Run by Wines of Argentina.

holidays.name: International Viognier Day
holidays.description: The aromatic white of Condrieu, now also grown in California and Australia.

holidays.name: International Qvevri Day
holidays.description: The buried clay vessel at the heart of Georgian winemaking, a UNESCO-listed practice.

holidays.name: World Marselan Day
holidays.description: A 1961 crossing of Cabernet Sauvignon and Grenache, increasingly seen as China's signature red.

holidays.name: International Sauvignon Blanc Day
holidays.description: Started by New Zealand Winegrowers, timed to the Marlborough harvest.

holidays.name: International Baga Day
holidays.description: Bairrada's tannic native red.

holidays.name: Oregon Wine Month
holidays.description: Month-long promotion by the Oregon Wine Board.

holidays.name: World Moscato Day
holidays.description: Muscat in all its forms, from Asti to Rutherglen.

holidays.name: Pinot Grigio Day
holidays.description: Italy's most exported white. One source puts this on 26 May instead.

holidays.name: National Mourvedre Day
holidays.description: Declared by Texas Wine Lover in 2017 to fill a gap in the calendar. The M in GSM; Monastrell in Spain.

holidays.name: International Chardonnay Day
holidays.description: Created by Rick Bakas, deliberately set on the Thursday before US Memorial Day weekend.

holidays.name: Anniversary of the Judgment of Paris
holidays.description: The 1976 blind tasting where California wines beat the best of Bordeaux and Burgundy in front of French judges, and the wine world rearranged itself.

holidays.name: National Wine Day
holidays.description: Wine in general, no qualifiers. Distinct from Global Drink Wine Day in February.

holidays.name: International Sommelier Day
holidays.description: A day for the people pouring rather than the wine itself.

holidays.name: National Bubbly Day
holidays.description: Sparkling wine of any origin.

holidays.name: Idaho Wine Month
holidays.description: Month-long promotion of Idaho wine.

holidays.name: Durif Day (Petite Sirah)
holidays.description: Claimed by the Riverina Winemakers Association in Australia. Durif and Petite Sirah are the same grape — a Syrah x Peloursin crossing.

holidays.name: World Verdejo Day
holidays.description: Rueda's white grape. Sources split between the second Friday and the second Thursday of June.

holidays.name: National Rose Day
holidays.description: The US rose day. Not the same as International Rose Day later in the month.

holidays.name: Prosecco Week
holidays.description: Sources disagree badly on this one — third week of June, 11-16 June, and 24-30 June all appear. Verify before relying on it.

holidays.name: English Wine Week
holidays.description: Set each year by WineGB: third Saturday of June through the last Sunday of June. Nine days despite the name.

holidays.name: Drink Chenin Blanc Day
holidays.description: Chenin from the Loire and South Africa. Dates in the wild range across 13, 14, 18 and 20 June — the third Saturday is the most defensible reading.

holidays.name: World Lambrusco Day
holidays.description: Emilia-Romagna's sparkling red, set on the summer solstice.

holidays.name: International Rose Day
holidays.description: The global rose day, as opposed to the US-focused National Rose Day two weeks earlier.

holidays.name: Sparkling Wine Week
holidays.description: Described only as 'the first week of July', which no source pins down precisely. Set here as 1-7 July.

holidays.name: International Cava Day
holidays.description: Spain's traditional-method sparkling wine. Most calendars say 12 July; one says the second Saturday of July.

holidays.name: International Shiraz Day
holidays.description: The Australian expression of Syrah, which has its own separate day in February.

holidays.name: National Wine & Cheese Day
holidays.description: Self-explanatory.

holidays.name: World Albarino Day
holidays.description: Rias Baixas' white grape. In Cambados the Festa do Albarino runs for roughly the first five days of August — the second-oldest wine festival in Spain.

holidays.name: Old Vine Day
holidays.description: Marks the founding of South Africa's Old Vine Project in 2016.

holidays.name: National White Wine Day
holidays.description: White wine of any kind.

holidays.name: National Verdelho Day
holidays.description: Declared by Tulloch Wines in 2025 for the Hunter Valley's Verdelho, on 8/8. New, and backed by a single winery — but a real, dated claim.

holidays.name: International Prosecco Day
holidays.description: Glera-based sparkling wine from Veneto and Friuli.

holidays.name: International Pinot Noir Day
holidays.description: Burgundy, Oregon, Central Otago and everywhere else that chases it.

holidays.name: National Red Wine Day
holidays.description: Red wine of any kind.

holidays.name: Cap Classique Day
holidays.description: South Africa's traditional-method sparkling wine, on the first day of Cape spring.

holidays.name: Bordeaux Wine Month (UK)
holidays.description: UK-wide trade promotion run by the Bordeaux wine council across 130+ merchants and bars.

holidays.name: International Cabernet Sauvignon Day
holidays.description: Created by Rick Bakas as the Labor Day counterpart to his Chardonnay Day. Some calendars instead list the first Thursday of September or a fixed 30 August — those are drifted retellings of this rule.

holidays.name: National Chianti Day
holidays.description: Tuscany's Sangiovese-based classic.

holidays.name: International Box Wine Day
holidays.description: Started in 2021 by Wine Nook. Bag-in-box, unapologetically.

holidays.name: National Port Wine Day
holidays.description: The more widely listed of the two Port days, promoted by Rota do Douro.

holidays.name: International Grenache Day
holidays.description: Confirmed by the Grenache Association itself: every third Friday of September. Garnacha in Spain.

holidays.name: National Wine Day of Moldova
holidays.description: Ziua Nationala a Vinului — the largest wine event in Eastern Europe, held on the first weekend of October in Chisinau. Established by government decree in 2002.

holidays.name: World Vranec Day
holidays.description: North Macedonia's dark, tannic native red.

holidays.name: International Orange Wine Day
holidays.description: Skin-contact white wine. One source dates it 5 October; 6 October is the more common listing.

holidays.name: Mexican Wine Day
holidays.description: Established in 2023 for the wines of Baja California and beyond.

holidays.name: Virginia Wine Month
holidays.description: Official month-long promotion by Virginia Wine.

holidays.name: Texas Wine Month
holidays.description: Month-long promotion of Texas wine.

holidays.name: Georgian Wine Month (UK)
holidays.description: UK-wide trade promotion by Wines of Georgia, launched each year on International Orange Wine Day.

holidays.name: Rioja Wine Month (UK)
holidays.description: UK retail and restaurant promotion of Rioja.

holidays.name: International Pinotage Day
holidays.description: South Africa's own crossing of Pinot Noir and Cinsault, created in 1925.

holidays.name: Drink Local Wine Week
holidays.description: Described as the 'second full week of October', which is ambiguous. Set here as the week starting the second Monday.

holidays.name: Prokupac Day
holidays.description: Serbia's flagship native red.

holidays.name: World Champagne Day
holidays.description: Run by the Comite Champagne. Distinct from National Champagne Day on 31 December.

holidays.name: International Mavrud Day
holidays.description: Bulgaria's native red, set on St Dimitar's Day.

holidays.name: International Carignan Day
holidays.description: Old-vine Carignan from the Languedoc, Priorat and Chile's Maule.

holidays.name: International Xinomavro Day
holidays.description: Greece's noble red from Naoussa and Amyndeon, often compared to Nebbiolo. Promoted by Wines of Greece.

holidays.name: International Sherry Week
holidays.description: Run by the Consejo Regulador of Jerez-Xeres-Sherry, with events in 30+ countries. First full week of November, Monday to Sunday.

holidays.name: International Merlot Day
holidays.description: Bordeaux's most-planted grape, still recovering its reputation from Sideways.

holidays.name: Wine in Moderation Day
holidays.description: European wine sector programme promoting responsible drinking.

holidays.name: St Martin's Day (Martinovanje)
holidays.description: The day St Martin traditionally turns the must into wine. One of the biggest wine holidays across Central Europe, marking the young wine's release.

holidays.name: International Tempranillo Day
holidays.description: Spain's flagship red, from Rioja and Ribera del Duero.

holidays.name: National Zinfandel Day
holidays.description: Run by ZAP, the Zinfandel Advocates and Producers.

holidays.name: Beaujolais Nouveau Day
holidays.description: The release of the year's Gamay, at 12:01am on the third Thursday of November. The date is set in French law.

holidays.name: International Carmenere Day
holidays.description: Created in 2014 for Chile's emblematic red, lost to phylloxera in Bordeaux and rediscovered in Chile in 1994 after decades mistaken for Merlot.

holidays.name: International Saperavi Day
holidays.description: Georgia's teinturier red — one of the few grapes with red flesh as well as red skin.

holidays.name: International Maratheftiko Day
holidays.description: Cyprus's rare native red.

holidays.name: International Cabernet Franc Day
holidays.description: Started by Social Vignerons to argue Cabernet Franc is more than a blending grape. Parent of both Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.

holidays.name: World Tokaj Aszu Day
holidays.description: Hungary's botrytised sweet wine from Tokaj, the world's first classified wine region (1730).

holidays.name: Pinot Meunier Day
holidays.description: The third and least-discussed of the three main Champagne grapes.

holidays.name: National Sangria Day
holidays.description: Sangria in the depths of December, for reasons nobody explains.

holidays.name: National Champagne Day
holidays.description: New Year's Eve. Distinct from World Champagne Day in October.
